# Tools: what to click
[textlink="Mining & Industry" link="CMUGuideIndustry"] · [textlink="Make these tools" link="CMUGuideIndustryRecipes"]
These are [bold]OOC controls[/bold]. Right-click equipment → [bold]Help[/bold] opens its instructions. Key names below follow your bindings.
## Digging kit
- [bold]Shovel:[/bold] hold it, point at clear nearby floor and press [keybind="ActivateItemInHand"] to dig a shaft. Right-click the tool to change up/down mode. - [bold]Pickaxe:[/bold] use the same shaft controls for deeper rock layers. To mine a wall, strike it with the appropriate mining tool. - [bold]Jackhammer:[/bold] the tool for black rock. Insert a charged power cell; a flat tool will refuse to work. - Wooden digging tools break after two digs; stone after six. Examine primitive tools to check their remaining uses.
[textlink="Where to dig, ladders and maps" link="CMUGuideIndustryDig"]
## Wood and fire
Chop a tree with an axe. Use a hand saw on its log to make planks. Logs occupy both hands. Use a stone striker on a fueled campfire or furnace; failed sparks are normal, but each attempt wears the striker.
## Powered tools and surveying
Insert a charged cell into powered tools; recharge spare cells in a powered charger. Electric screwdrivers, wrenches, cutters, crowbars and hammers perform their usual tool jobs faster.
Hold the [bold]prospector[/bold] and press [keybind="ActivateItemInHand"]. It spends charge to report nearby ore/oil deposit counts and the nearest direction and distance. It is a local scan, not a full map of unexplored caves.
